To carry a custom Lead field's data to the Contact on conversion, create a custom Contact field of a compatible type and map the Lead field to it in Object Manager > Lead > Fields & Relationships > Map Lead Fields. Conversion then copies the value automatically. Rule of thumb: custom lead field → map to a custom field.

translate.situation: Bring a custom lead value onto the new contact.
translate.see: The value appears on the contact automatically after conversion.
translate.notOther: Custom lead fields can't map to standard fields; a flow or task is unnecessary.

cards.traps: Custom-to-standard mapping is never allowed; custom maps only to custom.
cards.strip: Custom Lead field onto Contact at conversion → map to custom Contact field.

wrong.Create a flow to update the field on the: A Flow could copy it, but lead field mapping is the built-in feature for exactly this.
wrong.Create a task for the User to update the: Asking users to retype data is error-prone and unnecessary when mapping is automatic.
wrong.Map the custom Lead field to a standard: Custom Lead fields can't be mapped to standard Contact fields.

cards.prompt: What is true about changing the default company locale?
options: The company locale will be applied as the default locale for new Users, but only the Administrator can change the personal locale of a User.
The company locale will be applied as the default locale for new Users, but any User can change their personal locale setting.
When changed, the company locale is applied to all Users.
The company locale will only be applied to as the default for new Users, and cannot be changed.
answer: The company locale will be applied as the default locale for new Users, but any User can change their personal locale setting.
cards.why: This tests company vs. personal settings. Company Information's default locale (which controls date, time, number and name formats) is the default given to new users; existing users keep their current setting. Each user can change their own locale in their personal settings, without an admin. Rule of thumb: company settings are defaults for new users; personal settings are per user.
cards.traps: Company default ≠ forced on everyone; existing users keep their own setting.
cards.strip: Company locale changed → default for new users; each user can change their own.

wrong.The company locale will be applied as th: Users can change their own locale; an admin isn't required.
wrong.When changed, the company locale is appl: Changing the company locale doesn't change existing users' personal settings.
wrong.The company locale will only be applied: The company locale can be changed by an admin at any time, and users can change theirs.

cards.prompt: Party Suppliers and More need a form that can be used by Sales Reps to enter Party information, such as the party schedule, venue, event size, and other related event information. This form should be launched from a button on the record page. When the form is saved, a record is created and a follow-up Task is created. Which of the following tools can be used to meet this requirement?
answer: Screen Flow
cards.why: This tests the flow type that shows a form to a user. A Screen Flow is the only flow type that displays screens, so it can collect party details through input fields, then use Create Records to make the event record and the follow-up Task. You add it to the record page as a quick action (button) so reps launch it from there. Rule of thumb: user fills out a form → Screen Flow.

translate.situation: Reps fill out a form from a button, then records get created.
translate.feature: Screen flow (launched by a quick action).
translate.see: A pop-up form; on Finish, the record and task are created.
translate.notOther: Record-triggered flows have no screens; they run on save.

cards.traps: Only Screen Flows have screens; every other flow type runs in the background.
cards.strip: Form from a button · creates records → Screen Flow (quick action).

wrong.Apex Triggered Flow: There's no 'Apex Triggered Flow' type; flows can call Apex, but no flow type is triggered by Apex like this.
wrong.Schedule-Triggered Flow: Schedule-triggered flows run in the background on a schedule and can't show a form.
wrong.Record-Triggered Flow: Record-triggered flows run in the background when a record changes; they can't show screens.

cards.prompt: A User reports they are locked out of Salesforce. You have confirmed they have had multiple failed login attempts by reviewing their User Detail record. How can you as a Salesforce Administrator help the User get back into Salesforce? Select 2.
options: Create a new password for the User, and send them the new password in an email.
Select the Reset Password button on the User detail record page.
Select the Freeze button on the User Detail record page.
Edit the User Detail record, and select the checkbox "Generate new password and notify user immediately".
answer: Select the Reset Password button on the User detail record page.
Edit the User Detail record, and select the checkbox "Generate new password and notify user immediately".
cards.why: This tests unlocking a locked-out user. Resetting a user's password also unlocks their account; you can click Reset Password on the user record, or edit the user and check 'Generate new password and notify user immediately'. Either way Salesforce emails the user a link to set a new password. (There's also an Unlock button, but it isn't offered here.) Admins never see or send passwords themselves. Rule of thumb: locked out → Unlock or Reset Password.
cards.traps: Freeze sounds like an admin user action but it stops logins; it doesn't restore them.
cards.strip: User locked out → Reset Password (button or 'generate new password' checkbox) or Unlock.

wrong.Create a new password for the User, and: Admins can't set a password and email it themselves; Salesforce sends a secure reset link instead.
wrong.Select the Freeze button on the User Det: Freeze blocks a user from logging in, the opposite of what's needed.

cards.prompt: How long is data stored in the Recycle Bin?
answer: Up to 15 days.
cards.why: This tests the Recycle Bin. Deleted records stay in the Recycle Bin for 15 days, during which they can be restored; after that they're permanently erased. The org's Recycle Bin also has a size limit (25 times the org's MB storage), and the oldest records are purged first if it fills up. Deleted custom fields also have a 15-day window. Rule of thumb: Recycle Bin = 15 days.
cards.traps: 15 is the number for both deleted records (Recycle Bin) and deleted custom fields.
cards.strip: Recycle Bin retention → 15 days.

30 days is a common guess but not Salesforce's Recycle Bin limit.
wrong.Up to 7 days: 7 days is too short; records stay 15 days.
60 days is too long; records stay 15 days.

cards.prompt: What should a System Administrator configure to provide each Sales Rep a dashboard that shows their current Opportunity pipeline?
options: Set a Dashboard filter to the current user.
Create a dashboard for each user.
Create a dashboard folder for each user.
Set the Dashboard Running User to the current user.
answer: Set the Dashboard Running User to the current user.
cards.why: This tests dynamic dashboards. A dashboard's running user decides whose data access it shows. Setting 'View Dashboard As' to 'The dashboard viewer' makes it dynamic, so one dashboard shows each rep only their own pipeline. Reps also need record access as usual. Rule of thumb: each viewer sees their own data → dynamic dashboard (running user = viewer).
cards.traps: Filters and folders look like personalization but don't change whose data is shown; the running user does.
cards.strip: Each rep sees own pipeline · one dashboard → dynamic dashboard (running user = viewer).

wrong.Set a Dashboard filter to the current us: Dashboard filters let viewers narrow by field values, but they don't automatically limit each rep to their own data.
One dashboard per user doesn't scale and is a maintenance burden.
Folders control who can see a dashboard, not whose data it shows.
